slots.practicalActivity: Draw your own 5-stage Procure-to-Pay flow diagram (requisition -> purchase order -> receipt -> invoice -> payment/posting), labeling which Oracle Fusion module and which named role (requester, buyer, receiving clerk, AP processor) owns each stage. Then open the Procurement and Payables work areas in your Oracle Fusion practice environment and map each one to the stage(s) it covers.
slots.deliverable: Your own labeled 5-stage P2P diagram plus a short written map of which practice-environment work area corresponds to each stage.

lessons.title: Procurement Setup Review: Business Units and Agents

slots.practicalActivity: In your practice environment, open Manage Business Units and Manage Procurement Agents and record what's already configured there (requisitioning BU, procurement BU, agent assignment). Then write your own plan for a single purchasing transaction you'll carry through this course -- list the five documents (requisition, PO, receipt, invoice, payment) you expect to create before you create any of them.
slots.deliverable: Notes on the real BU/procurement-agent setup you found, plus your own written 5-document transaction plan.

slots.practicalActivity: In Self Service Procurement, create your own requisition the way Dana Whitfield builds hers: search the catalog for an item, add it to your cart with a quantity, confirm the header defaults (preparer, requisitioning business unit, deliver-to location), set a need-by date, and submit it.
slots.deliverable: One submitted requisition in your practice environment with a requisition number, confirmed header defaults, and a completed catalog line.

slots.practicalActivity: Track your Slot 3 requisition through the approval workflow (or review the approval rule that would apply to it), then open its distribution and identify which expense account and cost center it defaulted to -- the same way Dana's bearing requisition defaults to the maintenance account on her plant's cost center.
slots.deliverable: A short writeup naming your requisition's approver/approval rule and its distribution account, noting where each value defaulted from.

slots.practicalActivity: Process your approved requisition line into a new purchase order the way Marcus Ibarra does with Dana's bearing requisition, confirming the supplier, supplier site, and payment terms carry over automatically from the requisition's catalog entry.
slots.deliverable: One purchase order created directly from your Slot 3-4 requisition, with supplier and payment terms confirmed as auto-populated.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter lab: without referring back to the lessons, run a second requisition end to end -- create it, let it route to approval, inspect its distribution, and convert it to a purchase order. Time yourself and note any step you had to look up.
slots.deliverable: A second, independently created requisition-to-purchase-order cycle, plus a short self-assessment listing any step that needed a lookup.

lessons.title: Purchase Order Types and Purchase Agreements

slots.practicalActivity: Compare a standard purchase order against a blanket purchase agreement in your practice environment (open an example of each, or review the setup screens for both). Then create your own standard PO for a one-time item, filling in supplier, line, schedule, and distribution the way Marcus does for the bearings.
slots.deliverable: One created standard purchase order with a complete schedule and distribution, plus written notes on when a blanket agreement would be used instead.

slots.practicalActivity: Submit your Slot 7 PO for approval and communicate it to the supplier. Then simulate a real-world change -- increase the quantity or push out the need-by date -- and process it as a formal change order, noting the revision number the PO receives.
slots.deliverable: Your approved and communicated PO, plus one processed change order against it with the resulting revision number recorded.

slots.practicalActivity: Walk your PO through its closing statuses the way Meridian's bearing PO closes in the full walkthrough -- Closed for Receiving, Closed for Invoicing, Finally Closed. If your PO can't yet close, document exactly which condition (receipt complete, invoice complete) is still open and why.
slots.deliverable: A status log showing your PO's progression through its closing stages, or a clear note on which closing condition is still outstanding.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a receipt against your purchase order for the full ordered quantity the way Priya Nandan receives the 50 bearings. If the item is routed for inspection, move it through the inspection queue to an accepted disposition.
slots.deliverable: One completed receipt in your practice environment, with inspection routing resolved to an accepted quantity.

slots.practicalActivity: Process a partial return against your receipt (reducing the accepted quantity) to see the correction flow. Then open Receipt Accounting and confirm the accrual journal it generated -- debit expense, credit uninvoiced receipts accrual -- matches the lesson's example.
slots.deliverable: One processed return/correction plus a written record of the receipt accrual journal lines it produced.

slots.practicalActivity: Enter an AP invoice referencing your purchase order and receipt, let 3-way matching run, and resolve the result (or deliberately enter a quantity mismatch first to see a hold, then correct it). Once validated, run a Payment Process Request that selects your invoice for payment.
slots.deliverable: One matched, validated, and paid invoice, with notes on whether it matched cleanly or needed a hold resolved first.

lessons.title: Following the Transaction into General Ledger

slots.practicalActivity: Drill your paid invoice's accounting into the General Ledger to confirm the three journals (accrual, invoice, payment) landed correctly. Then perform your own AP-trial-balance-to-GL reconciliation and accrual reconciliation on this transaction, confirming the accrual account nets to zero.
slots.deliverable: A reconciliation memo for your transaction covering AP-to-GL tie-out and a zeroed-out accrual balance.

slots.practicalActivity: Deliberately break one checkpoint in a new transaction (for example, submit an invoice for a quantity greater than what was received) and troubleshoot it back to its source, documenting each diagnostic step you took.
slots.deliverable: A troubleshooting log for one deliberately broken transaction, from symptom to root cause to fix.

slots.practicalActivity: Replay your own transaction end to end in one sitting, listing every document number and journal in order the way the lesson replays LTV's bearing purchase. Then pick one exception scenario (a cancelled PO with a partial receipt, a short-shipped delivery) and resolve it in your practice environment.
slots.deliverable: A complete one-page document/journal chain for your transaction, plus one resolved exception scenario.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can run a complete Procure-to-Pay cycle in Oracle Fusion Cloud -- from requisition through purchase order, receiving, invoice matching, payment, and GL reconciliation -- and troubleshoot a break at any checkpoint.
